chunks: And through it, from al-Hasan, from Karram al-Khath'ami, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'By Allah, if there were bands on your mouths, I would tell every one of you what is for him. By Allah, if I found the pious among you, I would speak. Allah is the One assisted by.'

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah, a title for Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)
key_terms.أَوْكِيَةً: bands or coverings (metaphor for silence or restriction)

ai.seo_question: Why did Imam al-Sadiq withhold knowledge from his companions?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Kitab al-Ghayba*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the concealment of esoteric knowledge was not due to divine restriction or personal reluctance, but rather the insufficient piety (*atqa*) of his contemporaries to safeguard it. The metaphor of 'bands on their mouths' (*awkiyah*) signifies that even if physically silenced, the truth would still be conveyed to each individual according to their capacity, highlighting the Shia principle of *taqiyya* (prudent concealment) as a protective measure for the faithful. This underscores the scholarly view that the Imam’s silence was a strategic preservation of the *Sirr* (secret) until the advent of the Mahdi.
